Its independent background contributes the Poisson generating functional; at z=1 the age integral is 1-psi(q(t)). The binder accounts for the extra one in the mean. Monotone differentiation from below is valid even with infinite second moment: the possibly singular integral is bounded by mu-psi'(q(t)), by changing variables from age to binding probability. Uniform convergence of the short-age marks then gives the normalized pgf psi'(z)/mu and reduces the mean to the difference quotient of psi'. If J=1 almost surely, the triggering-batch sibling term vanishes identically. For the tail exponent between one and two, the rescaled sum has integrable bounds proportional to x^(-alpha) min(x,1), and integration by parts gives Gamma(2-alpha)/(alpha-1). At alpha=2, truncating at j=floor(1/F) and replacing 1-(1-F)^(j-1) by (j-1)F costs O(F) including the upper tail; the lower sum has leading c F log(1/F). The erfc asymptotic and the bounds exp(-dt)P(H<=t)<=F(t)<=P(H<=t) give the displayed constants. Finite ordinary mean follows by domination by total production.
